title: Embeddings & vector stores
summary: Chunks become vectors, vectors go into a store, and a question's vector finds its nearest chunks. This module measures every choice on the way: **which embedding model** (two local, one multilingual, one API), **which language** the question is in (Nimbus customers write in Hindi, Tamil and Hinglish), **which store** (Chroma, FAISS, pgvector), how an index stays **in sync** with changing documents, and how ingestion survives **scale**: batches, duplicates, bad records and crashes. Production keeps the local model, adds query translation (multilingual questions found: 4/10 → 10/10) and an HNSW index.
learn: **Embeddings**: embed_query and embed_documents, cosine similarity, and choosing a model on your own questions
**Multilingual retrieval**: a multilingual model, an API model, or translating the question
**Vector stores and Chroma**: add, search with scores, MMR, filters, persist, update and delete
**FAISS**: distance strategies, saving and loading, and exact vs approximate (HNSW) search
**pgvector**: production's index, the same search in SQL, and an HNSW index
**Index sync and ingestion at scale**: record managers, batching, concurrency, deduplication, dead letters, resuming
flow:
INGEST   chunks ─embed_documents─→ vectors ─→ pgvector table (+ HNSW index) ← record manager: hash per chunk, per source
QUERY    question ─(non-ASCII? translate to English: 1 cached chat call)─→ embed_query ─→ nearest k by cosine distance

labs.explain:
An **embedding** turns text into a vector; texts with similar meaning get vectors pointing the same way. The lab shows what `embed_query` and `embed_documents` return and how cosine similarity ranks them, then measures four models on production's chunks and all 45 questions: **bge-small** (local, 384 dims), **bge-base** (local, 768), **multilingual MiniLM** (local, 384) and **mistral-embed** (API, 1024): quality, speed and index size.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Questions use query_embed: bge adds its search instruction.
mistral-embed: 1024 dimensions, so a separate table.

labs.explain:
Ten questions in Hindi, Tamil, Hinglish, Spanish, French and German against English documents, four ways: the **English-only** model, a **multilingual** model, the **API** model, and **translating the question** first (also restricted to non-ASCII questions, production's policy). Then an answer in the user's own language.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.match: return any(not c.isascii() and c.isalpha() for c in question)
notes.text: Devanagari, Tamil and accented letters trigger translation; ASCII Hinglish doesn't.
The same question is asked again and again: translate it once.

labs.explain:
Every LangChain vector store has the same interface: add documents, search (with scores, with MMR for diversity), delete by id. The lab uses it with the in-memory store and with **Chroma**, a local database that persists to disk: reopen without re-embedding, distance vs relevance scores, metadata filters (`$lt`, `$and`, `$in`), and reads, updates and deletes without searching.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

**FAISS** is a vector search library: build an index from production's chunks, search with L2 or cosine, save and load (with pickle's warning), merge and delete. Then raw FAISS on 20,000 vectors: **exact** search (compares everything) against **HNSW** (walks a graph), with the speed and recall of each `efSearch`.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Candidates explored per query: the recall/speed dial.

labs.explain:
Production's own index: **pgvector** stores vectors in a Postgres column. The lab searches it through LangChain, runs the same search in SQL with the `<=>` operator (same distances), and shows the query plan walking the **HNSW index** production created.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

code.why: Production: an HNSW index, created once.

notes.text: Idempotent: every start checks, only the first creates.

labs.explain:
Re-running ingestion must not duplicate chunks or leave stale ones behind. LangChain's `index()` with a **record manager** remembers a hash of every chunk per source: unchanged chunks are skipped, edited ones replaced, and removed sources deleted (`cleanup="full"`).

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: A full run is the whole corpus: anything missing is deleted.

labs.explain:
A messy export of support tickets (empty rows, pasted logs, re-exported copies) through a pipeline that streams in **batches**, embeds **concurrently** with a limit, removes **duplicates**, sets bad records aside in a **dead-letter** list, and **resumes** after a simulated crash without duplicating anything.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Progress recorded only after a batch is written.

path.title: Production path: Nimbus retrieval v2
path.summary: Four embedding models and two query policies were measured on all 45 questions and a 10-question multilingual set. Production keeps **bge-small** (local, free, private, 4 ms per question) and adds a **Retriever** that translates non-English questions to English first (one cached chat call): multilingual questions found 4/10 → 10/10 with English quality unchanged. The pgvector table gets an **HNSW index**, and the embedding provider becomes a setting.

steps.title: Embedding model
steps.tagline: Local by default, API as a setting
steps.explain: `get_embeddings(settings)` returns the configured model. bge-small stays the default: on production's chunks it matched bge-base and beat the multilingual model on English. mistral-embed was best on English (hit@5 0.93 vs 0.89) but costs a network request per question (~1.5 s here), shares the chat model's rate limit, and sends text to the provider; switching also means re-embedding into a 1024-dimension table.
production: Changing the embedding model invalidates every vector: re-embed into a new table and switch over, never mix models in one index.
Record the model name with the index (table name or metadata) so a mismatch fails loudly.

steps.title: Retriever
steps.explain: The new `Retriever` is the one place questions are searched. It prepares the query first: by policy, a question with non-ASCII letters is translated to English (cached by question), then embedded and searched. Later modules add filters, hybrid search and reranking here.

notes.match: if model is not None and needs_translation(question, policy):
notes.text: Only when the policy says so: English questions cost nothing extra.

production: Log the original and the translated query together: a bad translation is otherwise invisible.
Answer in the user's language (Module 7's prompt does this).

steps.title: HNSW index
steps.explain: `VectorIndex` creates an HNSW index on the embedding column once (m=16, ef_construction=64). At 99 chunks Postgres may still scan the table; the index pays off as the corpus grows, at a small recall cost that `hnsw.ef_search` controls.
production: Build the index after a bulk load, not before: inserting into an HNSW index is slower than building it.
Watch recall when tuning ef_search: measure against an exact search on a sample.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Measured on production chunks:

| configuration | hit@5 (45) | MRR | multilingual top-3 (10) | per question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bge-small | 0.89 | 0.705 | 0.4 | free |
| **bge-small + translate non-ASCII** | **0.89** | **0.705** | **1.0** | a chat call for 7 of 10 |
| bge-base | 0.89 | 0.687 | 0.5 | free |
| multilingual MiniLM | 0.82 | 0.669 | 0.8 | free |
| mistral-embed | 0.93 | 0.756 | 0.8 | an API request |
production: Add every question that failed in production to the multilingual set, in the language it was asked.
Re-run when the chat model changes: translation quality moves with it.
